Layouts
-------

A layout presents a value in one machine word. It is declared once, in a
module, and every tool reads that declaration: the checker, the Lean
admission, and the C generator.

  cesta layout check MODULE THEORY
  cesta layout functions MODULE THEORY
  cesta layout header MODULE THEORY -o OUTPUT.h

check reads the layouts a theory declares, refuses malformed ones with a
reason, and prints each accepted layout in a normalized form. header writes
ordinary C accessors for every layout of the theory; functions prints the
same accessors as recorded expressions.

Declaration
-----------

A layout theory declares each layout as an equation:

  Theory Frames() {
    Empty Equations {
      (FrameIdentity) == (Layout "cesta-layout/1"
        (Word 32)
        (Constants (Const ClassOneFirst (Pow2 20)) ...)
        (Fields (Field handle "value") (Field generation "value"))
        (Case (Prefix 1 0)
          (Place handle (Bits 0 20) (Range 1 (Minus ClassOneFirst 1)))
          (Place generation (Bits 20 11) (Range 1 2046)))
        ...
        (Reserved (Prefix 4 15)
          (Place handle (Bits 0 28) (Offset HandleLimit))
          (Place generation (Bits 28 0)))
        (Location "immutable"));
    }
  }

Word        the word's width, 1 to 64 bits.
Constants   named constants. An expression is a decimal integer, a constant,
            (Hex "..."), (Pow2 E), (Sum E ...), (Times E ...) or (Minus A B),
            exact in 64 bits.
Fields      the value's fields, in order, each with a kind: "value",
            "any-child", "all-children", "fact", "cache", "occurrence" or
            "reference". A field written after the word is shared says
            (Written "after-publication").
Case        a case of the word: an optional (Prefix LENGTH VALUE) on the top
            bits, then a Place for every field in the bits below. A place
            stores the value minus its Offset (default 0) and admits the
            values in its Range (default: every value its bits hold).
Reserved    a case that reads words but admits no value.
Alias       (Alias NAME FIELD CONDITION): a second name for a field, with the
            condition under which the two must be split.
Requires    (Requires (AtMost FIELD BITS) REASON): a bound some consumer of
            the field relies on.
Location    the word's write discipline: "immutable", "single-owner",
            "construction" or "atomic".
From        (From OLD): this layout is a newer version of the layout OLD,
            declared earlier in the theory. It must read the same fields in
            the same order, and each admitting case of OLD must lie inside
            one admitting case of this layout, so every old word has a new
            word.
Key         (Key FIELD): FIELD chooses the case. Its ranges must ascend
            through the admitting cases in prefix order, each lying wholly
            below the next, so a value's case is the one whose range holds
            its FIELD.

Checks
------

A layout is refused when:
  - a field lies outside the bits below its case's prefix, two fields of a
    case overlap, or a bit below the prefix is in no field;
  - a case prefix extends or is shared with another, or some words are in no
    case (declare those Reserved);
  - a range admits nothing or does not fit its offset and bits;
  - two cases admit a common value, or read some words as the same value;
  - a field is undeclared, missing from a case, placed twice, or has an
    unknown kind;
  - an alias names no field or gives no condition, or a requirement does not
    hold in some case;
  - a field written after publication shares a word that is not atomic;
  - a field name would name another accessor;
  - a word with several cases carries a field of a derived kind;
  - a key names no field, or its ranges do not ascend through the admitting
    cases in prefix order.

Normalized form
---------------

  (cesta-layout/1 NAME WIDTH (Fields (FIELD KIND WRITTEN) ...) TRIE
    (Location DISCIPLINE) (Aliases (NAME FIELD CONDITION) ...)
    (Requires (FIELD BITS REASON) ...) [(From OLD)] [(Key FIELD)]
    [(Constants (Const NAME VALUE EXPRESSION) ...)])

  TRIE ::= (Leaf "admits"|"reserved" (Place SHIFT WIDTH OFFSET LO HI) ...)
         | (Node TRIE TRIE)

Constants are evaluated, and listed with their values and expressions;
prefixes become a binary trie whose leaves are the cases, and every case
lists its places in field order.

Accessors
---------

For a layout NAME with fields F1 ... Fn in a word of 8, 16, 32 or 64 bits,
header writes static inline functions:

  uint64_t NAME_F(uintW_t word)        the field's value, for every word
  bool NAME_valid(uintW_t word)         the word is one a value is written as
  bool NAME_admits(uint64_t F1, ...)    some case admits the value
  uintW_t NAME_encode(uint64_t F1, ...) the value's word (0 when none admits it)

A newer version gets NAME_from_OLD(old), the new word for an old word, or 0
for a word OLD does not decode. Zero may also be a successful encoded word;
test OLD_valid(old) to distinguish refusal from success. A single-case word also gets
NAME_set_F(word, value). A single-case word
with derived kinds gets NAME_derive_init(), NAME_derive_child(acc, child)
and NAME_derive_finish(acc, own), which build a parent's word from its
children's, and NAME_value_copy, NAME_store and NAME_relocate, which keep
exactly the kinds each operation keeps: storing drops occurrence marks.

Every declared constant C is exported as #define NAME_C UINT64_C(VALUE).

Views follow the accessors. A word with several cases gets, for each field,

  uint64_t NAME_F_lo(uintW_t word)       the field's lower bound in the word's case
  uint64_t NAME_F_hi(uintW_t word)       its upper bound there

A layout with (Key K) gets, for each field,

  uint64_t NAME_F_lo_for_K(uint64_t K)   the field's lower bound in the case
                                          whose range holds K (0 when none does)
  uint64_t NAME_F_hi_for_K(uint64_t K)   its upper bound there
  bool NAME_admits_K(uint64_t K)          some case's range holds K

A keyed layout, or one with a single admitting case, gets

  uintW_t NAME_pack(uint64_t F1, ...)     the word of an admitted value

pack checks nothing: it compares the key once per case and writes each
field minus its offset into its slot. For a value NAME_admits accepts it
returns what NAME_encode returns; for any other value its result is
unspecified, though never undefined behavior. Call it where the value is
known to be admitted, and NAME_encode elsewhere.

A word whose location is "atomic" is accessed only atomically:
NAME_atomic_load acquires, NAME_atomic_store releases, and a single-case
word gets NAME_atomic_set_F, which replaces the field by compare-and-swap of
the whole word through NAME_set_F, so writers of different fields never lose
each other's updates.

Each body is one expression over uint64_t: constants, &, |, ~, shifts by
constants below 64, +, -, ==, <= and ?:. A narrower word is converted to
uint64_t before use, so no integer promotion changes a value, and a bound
that always holds is written as 1.

Evidence
--------

MeTTapedia's LayoutCodes proves, once, for every layout that is well formed:
a written value reads back; a word that reads as a value is the one word that
value is written as; and distinct words read as distinct values, valid or
not. The admission decodes each printed layout in the Lean kernel and decides
that it is well formed, so these laws hold of the layout the module actually
declares. A malformed printed layout is decided not admitted.

For CeTTa's frame identities, MeTTapedia also proves that the declared layout
is the codec CeTTa uses: the same total reading, the same checked reading and
the same words.

MeTTapedia's LayoutLowering states C's meaning of the accessor expressions
(unsigned 64-bit arithmetic, a shift by 64 or more undefined) and proves, for
every well-formed layout, that the accessors compute the layout's reading of
each field, its checked reading, its encoding, its single-field writes, the
derived word of a parent (folded child by child) and each operation's word.
The admission decides, for every declared layout, that the accessors Cesta
records are exactly that lowering; an accessor with one wrong mask bit is
refused. LayoutKinds proves what the kinds mean over whole terms: a summary
bit is set exactly when some (every) leaf has it, so a missing bit proves
absence, and a derived node never carries an occurrence mark.

The header also names each non-atomic field, validity, encoding, kind and
view accessor expression CESTA_LAYOUT_NAME_BODY. Migration is function-only.
BODY formals use private positional names. Printed field parameters use the
cesta_value_ prefix, so legal logical names such as uint64_t, UINT64_C and
C keywords cannot capture the C type or literal helpers. Function records
retain the logical parameter names; expression variables are indexed, so
this change of C binder spelling preserves their positions.
The public typed inline function wraps that expression and evaluates each
call argument once. The BODY macro is an implementation interface for C11
external-linkage inline adapters, which cannot refer to a static function.
Use BODY only with already-evaluated, nonvolatile parameters or local values
of the accessor's declared types. It may repeat or omit parameter reads;
it promises neither evaluation count nor order for arbitrary expressions.
Perform volatile and atomic loads before passing their values to BODY.

Admission checks the normalized declaration's field kinds, write phases,
location, aliases and width requirements as well as the unsigned expression
records. This checks declared conditions. It does not establish ownership,
sharing or race freedom of a C program using those declarations. Atomic load,
store and compare-and-swap wrappers remain outside the unsigned expression
model. A separate test-layout-bridge gate checks the actual CeTTa codec bridge;
test-layout-admission first rebuilds the layout models it imports.

The generated headers compile without warnings under GCC and Clang, in c11
and gnu11, with -Wall -Wextra -Werror -pedantic, and agree with an
independent reading of the normalized layouts on boundary and random words.
At a pinned CeTTa revision, CeTTa's own frame-identity decoder agrees with
the generated reading and validity on every 32-bit word, and its spelling
with the generated encoding on every valid identity.

MeTTapedia's LayoutViews proves, for every well-formed layout, that the
bound views compute the bounds of the word's case and that a decoded value
lies within them; that under an ascending key a value has a word exactly
when the case its key selects admits it, and the key views compute that
case's bounds and whether it exists; and that for an admitted value pack
writes the value's word. The admission decides, for every declared layout,
that the recorded views are exactly these, that the key ascends, and that
the exported constants are the declared ones, each re-evaluated from its
expression; a pack with a wrong case boundary, a wrong constant and a
descending key are refused.

MeTTapedia's LayoutMigration proves, for a newer version that embeds the
older one, that a migrated word reads back as the old word's value, that
exactly the old version's invalid words are refused, and that distinct old
words never share a new word; the admission decides that the recorded
NAME_from_OLD is that migration's lowering.

Four threads writing one atomic word through its accessors neither race nor
lose updates under ThreadSanitizer, under GCC and Clang; the same writes on a
plain word are reported as a data race, which is why such a word is refused.

Not proved: that GCC and Clang compile the accessor expressions as C defines
them; that the printed C is the recorded expression; the C11 memory model
behind the atomic accessors. All three are tested as above.
